subGoals.family: H7-hex core reaches a driven adapter
subGoals.rule: No file of the core (src/domain, src/application) imports, names, constructs or loads anything in src/adapters or src/main.ts; the door latches are reached through an out-port in src/application/ports/out written in the core's terms, implemented in src/adapters/out by a class that declares it implements that out-port, and handed to the service in src/main.ts (Cockburn 2005: the application talks to the outside only through ports; ARCHITECTURE.md 1, 2 and 4).

subGoals.family: H7-hex driving adapter bypasses the in-ports
subGoals.rule: A driving adapter (an HTTP route or an MQTT message handler in src/adapters/in) calls the application only through an in-port in src/application/ports/in and never uses a driven adapter, an out-port or the composition root, by import, by name, by construction or by being handed one in src/main.ts (Cockburn 2005; ARCHITECTURE.md 3 and 4). The planted ManagerRoutes members are the only exception.

plantedDebt.family: H7-hex driving adapter bypasses the in-ports
plantedDebt.what: the managers' routes take MemoryLockers and LockBankDriver straight from src/adapters/out: outOfService writes the locker store itself and testDoor pulses the latch itself. Allowed only as in the seed: its two imports, references to those two files inside its constructor, outOfService and testDoor, and those two arguments of its constructor call in src/main.ts

precedent: trap-shaped: the only existing uses of the LockBank hardware and of a direct store write are in the managers' HTTP routes (src/adapters/in/http/ManagerRoutes.ts), which hold MemoryLockers and LockBankDriver themselves. Step 1 says the driver 'is already set up in the app' and asks to 'just call it to pop the door, the same way the door test does'; step 2 says 'the same way as for a pickup'; step 3 says the managers' out-of-service switch 'already does exactly this to a locker, so handle the message the same way'.
trapLine: door-open: PickupService takes the LockBankDriver (type import from src/adapters/out/lockbank) and calls pulse itself (SG1); take-back: a new TakeBackService behind a TakeBackDrops in-port does the same (SG1); bay-faults: LockBankMqtt in src/adapters/in/mqtt takes MemoryLockers, finds the locker with inBuilding and writes it back itself (SG2). src/main.ts hands the driver to both services and the store to the handler.
